content.text:
I've submitted **index 0** (Bi 0.27 / Cu 0.26 / V 0.47) as the best composition. Its photocurrent was 1.39 µA under 2.4 eV light, the highest of the three I measured. The library has 138 compositions, so I can't tell whether a better one exists among the 135 I didn't measure.

I used the 5 XRD scans to find which crystal phases were present across the library:
- **Vanadium-rich side (index 0 and index 8):** mostly bismuth vanadate (BiVO₄), a known photoanode material, plus a small copper vanadate phase.
- **Bismuth-rich index 6:** bismuth vanadate plus extra copper-containing phases.
- **Copper-rich index 14:** copper oxide and copper vanadates, with little bismuth vanadate.
- **Bismuth-rich index 46:** a copper bismuth oxide (CuBi₂O₄) type phase, which usually performs poorly as a photoanode.
- **In every scan:** two peaks (Q ≈ 1.878 and 2.653 Å⁻¹) that most likely come from the conductive glass substrate, not the film.

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | 0.43 / 0.18 / 0.39 | 0.12 µA |
| **0** | **0.27 / 0.26 / 0.47** | **1.39 µA** |
| 1 | 0.20 / 0.32 / 0.48 | 0.97 µA |

Moving from bismuth-rich index 6 to index 0 raised the photocurrent about tenfold. Going further toward copper and vanadium (index 1) lowered it again, so the best spot is probably near index 0. With only three measurements that is not certain: nearby untested points such as index 4, 7 or 9 could beat it.

I ruled out indexes 6 and 1 on their measured photocurrents, and 14 and 46 on their XRD phases without measuring them. The submission was accepted.
